target_customer: Crypto holders and borrowers (at founding), later US retail users buying tokens with bank money
problem: Lending and borrowing crypto, and later moving dollars between bank accounts and decentralized exchanges, required clumsy and risky manual steps.
business_model: Protocol and app for peer to peer crypto lending, later a consumer wallet with fees on token purchases
product_category: Decentralized finance lending protocol and Ethereum smart wallet

founders.name: Nadav Hollander
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO of Dharma Labs; he became CTO of OpenSea after the 2022 acquisition. Education and earlier employers not found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building lending contracts on Ethereum in 2017 meant writing new smart contract protocols with security risk and little tooling, hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open protocols and code were forkable; liquidity was the only possible moat and later Dharma moved to build on Compound, which suggests it could not hold its own liquidity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it directly in 2017. The app was later acquired by OpenSea in January 2022 and the wallet was shut within a month.

market_need_then: Crypto lending and borrowing demand was emerging in 2017 alongside the ICO boom, but sources opened do not quantify demand at the time.

branding.domain_note: Used dharma.io; the domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page after the shutdown.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer pitch later compared itself to Coinbase on steroids (YC description).

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself was found; coverage focused on the product and the sale.

pivots.from: Own peer to peer lending protocol
pivots.to: Fixed rate lending built on the Compound protocol
pivots.why: Press said Dharma and Compound had been competitors before Dharma moved to build on Compound.

pivots.to: Consumer Ethereum wallet linked to US bank accounts
pivots.why: Not stated in opened sources; the YC description shows the wallet as the product by the time of acquisition. Year approximate.

outcome_analysis: Dharma raised a 7 million dollar Series A in February 2019 from crypto focused investors and pivoted from its own lending protocol toward Compound based fixed rate loans and then a consumer wallet. OpenSea acquired it in January 2022 for an undisclosed price, with an Axios report of 110 to 130 million dollars unconfirmed, and used it to add engineering talent and a CTO. The wallet app was shut within a month, so this reads as a talent led exit during the 2021 crypto boom.
notes: Series A investor list is from a search summary of CoinDesk, CoinGeek and Cypherhunter listings; I opened none of them successfully. Founding competitors are not listed because competitor sources found were dated 2019 or later (Compound, MakerDAO, EthLend). Acquisition price unverified (Axios speculation only). Other co-founders were not found in opened sources. Seed funding before 2019 not found; CB Insights total of about 7.37M is aggregator only.
